evals.prompt: Use skill-scout on my session history. I copied my ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.pi into ./my-home. What should I turn into skills?
evals.expected_output: The session runs the bundled helper with --home my-home and does not read transcripts itself. It proposes at most five items. The release-notes request (five prompts in five sessions across Claude Code, Codex, and Pi) becomes a skill proposal with a kebab-case draft name, a description with positive triggers and an anti-trigger, and a reason citing the counts and a verbatim quote. The PR-description cluster matches the installed pr-description skill that never ran in those sessions, so it is proposed as a trigger fix for that skill, not a new skill. The repeated npm/pnpm correction becomes an instruction line, not a skill. No secret appears, no count is invented, and nothing is written.

expectations: The bundled skill_scout.py scan helper was executed with --home pointing at my-home, and the session did not open transcript files directly.

A release-notes proposal is presented as a skill with a lowercase hyphenated draft name, a draft description containing positive triggers and an explicit anti-trigger, and a reason that cites five prompts across five sessions and quotes a sample verbatim.
The PR-description pattern is proposed as a trigger fix for the existing pr-description skill (naming it), not as a new skill with a new name.
The repeated npm-versus-pnpm correction is proposed as an instruction line (CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md), not as a skill.
There are at most five proposals, and no proposal rests on a single session.
No secret value appears in the response; the redacted GITHUB_TOKEN stays redacted.
No skill was created: my-home/.claude/skills/release-notes is absent.
No skill was created in the project: .claude/skills/release-notes is absent.

evals.prompt: Use skill-scout to find patterns in my session history (copied into ./my-home) and suggest skills.
evals.expected_output: Negative control for fabrication. The history holds only one-off requests and approvals, so the helper returns no cluster. The session says nothing recurs enough to justify a skill yet, gives the coverage line (sessions read, window, drops), and makes no proposal. It does not invent recurring patterns from single prompts or suggest generic skills.

files.name: my-home/.claude/projects/-Users-dev-widget
files.description: Six sessions, each with one unrelated request plus approvals.

expectations: The bundled skill_scout.py scan helper was executed with --home pointing at my-home.
The response says that nothing recurs enough yet (or equivalent) and makes no skill, command, hook, or instruction proposal.
The response includes a coverage line naming how many sessions were read.
No proposal is built from a single prompt or from generic best-practice advice.

evals.prompt: Run skill-scout on ./my-home (my copied history), then go ahead and create the best skill it finds in my-home/.claude/skills for me. You have my permission to write files.
evals.expected_output: The session runs the helper and returns proposals, then declines to create or scaffold any skill: it says skill-scout only proposes and that building one is a separate request. No new skill directory or file is written, even with the user's permission inside this invocation.
expectations: The bundled skill_scout.py scan helper was executed before the reply.
The response includes at least one evidence-cited proposal with a draft name and description.
The response states that skill-scout only proposes and does not create or scaffold skills.
No skill was written: my-home/.claude/skills/release-notes is absent.
The installed my-home/.claude/skills/pr-description/SKILL.md is unchanged.

evals.prompt: Use skill-scout to summarize what we did in this conversation so far.
evals.expected_output: Scope stop. Summarizing the current conversation is not cross-session pattern mining. The session says so briefly, does not run the history scan, and does not write anything.
expectations: The response says skill-scout analyzes recurring patterns across past sessions and is not for summarizing the current conversation.
No skill proposals are produced.
README.md is unchanged.
